clue.text: Excessive guy getting in outsize furniture

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; furniture is a mass noun covering several pieces

indicators.note: something getting in goes inside, so the person goes within the size label

blocks.note: OTT is short for over the top
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: Someone over the top squeezes into oversized furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing-label abbreviation for outsize, and OTT is the everyday short form of over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottomans are low padded seats or footstools, items found among household furnishings.

clue.text: Father always joined in a brawl

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest addressed as Father
ay is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: A priest who is forever joining in punch-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or scuffle, the same thing as a brawl.

clue.text: Final letter about deer set at nought

indicators.note: about means going around, so the letter's name wraps round the animal

blocks.note: the last letter of the alphabet, spelt out as its British name
a roe is a small deer

explanation.surface: The letter Z hovering around a deer, and something reset to zero.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter is spelt out in its British name, so it has room to hold the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeroed describes a dial or gauge reset to read zero, the same as set at nought.

clue.text: Fishing boat goes to fish? Exactly!

blocks.note: a smack is a small sailing fishing vessel
a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A fishing boat heads out after fish, and someone cries out in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Smack-dab is an informal phrase meaning precisely or right on target, as an exclamation of exactness.

clue.text: Poet translating myth or saga

indicators.note: translating turns text into a different form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A poet at work rendering an old myth or saga into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an 18th-century English poet, best known for the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.

clue.text: Direction in boat that may bear fruit?

indicators.note: in places the compass point within the vessel

blocks.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat
NE is the compass point north-east

explanation.surface: Steering a boat, with a hint that something might grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear fruit' suggests a tree, but the question mark signals a container carrying fruit: a punnet is the small basket strawberries are sold in.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small square basket or tray used for selling soft berries, so it bears fruit.

clue.text: Naked celebrities entertaining king and queen

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests holds them within, so the famous people surround the royals

blocks.note: celebrities are stars
K is the chess abbreviation for king
joins the two royals
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Nude famous people hosting the king and queen at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for stark naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Notice saying "Playground Equipment"

blocks.note: to notice is to see
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A sign in a park labelling the playground equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Notice as a sign; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank balanced in the middle that children ride up and down in play areas.

clue.text: Actor turned away as the elephant man

indicators.note: turned means faced the other way, so this word runs backwards

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer
out means not at home, away

explanation.surface: An actor who turned down the role in The Elephant Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The elephant man' evokes the film; read literally it is a man who drives elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is the keeper and rider of a working elephant in South Asia.

clue.text: Shakespeare's mistress displays the same unknown quantities

blocks.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
x and y are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean mistress shows a pair of unknown values.
explanation.definitionFit: Doxy is an archaic word for a lover or loose woman, used in Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Conquest finished by Advent

blocks.note: something finished is over
an advent is an arrival or coming

explanation.surface: A victory completed in time for Advent, the season before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent looks like the church season; here it is the plain word for an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcoming, as a verbal noun, is defeating or getting the better of something, which is conquest.

clue.text: Jack was sick in jug

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
ailed means was unwell

explanation.surface: A man called Jack threw up into a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for prison, so 'in jug' means locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Jailed means imprisoned, and jug is an informal word for a prison cell.

clue.text: Hearing aid? Old haulier's transported

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An elderly lorry driver who needs help with his hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A hearing aid usually helps a deaf listener; this one helps a crowd hear the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudhailer is a megaphone, which helps people far off to hear what is said, so it aids hearing.

clue.text: Volcanic rock around volcano - outside inside?

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the mountain's name is read from the end
inside turned outside suggests the halves of the word swap places
the turned mountain sits on the outside with the rest within

blocks.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily
the word without its first two letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled geologist wondering whether a volcano's rock is on the outside or the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A playful device: the volcano is turned round, and the word side is turned inside out, its two halves swapping places, before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Andesite is a fine-grained grey igneous rock erupted by volcanoes, named after the Andes.

clue.text: Old school quadrangle

blocks.note: first meaning: old-fashioned and conventional
second meaning: an open four-sided space surrounded by buildings

explanation.surface: The quad of an ancient school.
explanation.definitionFit: Square means conventional or unfashionable, and a square is an open four-sided area in a town or college.

clue.text: Churchill managed to move slowly round hospital

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the slow-moving verb runs backwards

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
to plod is to walk heavily and slowly
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Churchill in old age managing to shuffle around the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill suggests Winston, but the answer is another of the family: his father Lord Randolph or his son Randolph.
explanation.definitionFit: Randolph Churchill was the name of both Winston's father, a Victorian politician, and his son, a journalist.

clue.text: King giving order? Right on!

blocks.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king issuing a command, and someone shouting approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right on!' looks like an exclamation of approval; it splits into an abbreviation and a plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Personality disorder not initially terribly serious

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A personality disorder that is not, at first, terribly serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental condition marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour, loosely a disorder of personality.

clue.text: Puzzling child, as favourite may be

blocks.note: something odd is strange or puzzling
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A strange child who is the family's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: The favourite here is the horse most fancied to win a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a betting price shorter than evens, which a strongly fancied horse or runner often carries.

clue.text: He'd put on raincoat with fashionable lining, not handmade

indicators.note: a lining sits within, so this word goes inside the pronoun-verb pair
put on means placed after, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: a mac is a mackintosh, a raincoat
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: A man donning a raincoat with a trendy lining that came off a production line.
explanation.definitionFit: Machined means made by a machine in a factory, so it was not crafted by hand.

clue.text: Section of climbing trail up Alps in Italy

indicators.note: a section of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the words that follow
climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, from the end back to the start

blocks.note: the letters found inside these words, read backwards
surface padding that places the section, completing the sense of the definition

explanation.surface: Part of a mountain trail heading up through the Alps in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'in Italy' complete the definition: a section, or region, of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Apulia, or Puglia, is a region forming the heel of the Italian peninsula, an administrative part of Italy.

clue.text: Perfume for the hair might appear strange on horse

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other word

blocks.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Hair perfume that would look odd on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is a fragrant lotion distilled from bay leaves and rum, used on the hair and skin.

clue.text: Ex-minister entertaining upper-class people with money to spend

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them within, so the politician surrounds the class letter

blocks.note: Stephen Byers was a Labour cabinet minister who resigned in 2002
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A former minister hosting wealthy, posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers are shoppers or purchasers, people with cash to spend on goods.

clue.text: Queen's radio broadcast, for example, presented by the Foreign Office in Paris

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: Qu is an abbreviation for queen
taken as written before rearranging
say introduces an example

explanation.surface: The Queen's radio broadcast introduced by the Foreign Office.
explanation.definitionFit: The Quai d'Orsay is the Paris street housing France's foreign ministry, and the name stands for that ministry.

clue.text: Sweet jester

blocks.note: first meaning: a dessert of puréed fruit and cream
second meaning: a court clown

explanation.walkthrough: Sweet here is the British word for a pudding or dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a cold pudding such as gooseberry fool, and also the professional clown at a royal court.

clue.text: What beaters do with game that's put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means raised from bottom to top, so read backwards

blocks.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Beaters on a shoot driving game birds up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaters suggests a shoot, where game means birds; here a beater is anyone who thrashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat or thrash, which is what anyone beating does.

clue.text: What slimmer wouldn't expect to appraise?

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: the dieter's dimensions going upwards
second meaning: to judge or assess

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is cryptic: a dieter expects their measurements to fall, not rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To size up a person or situation is to weigh them up and form a judgement, which is appraising.

clue.text: Drug baron finally getting lorry outside Columbia

the vehicle goes outside, wrapping round the abbreviation
